composing_text: 8th Infantry Brigade; 9th Infantry Brigade; 185th Infantry Brigade
current_activity: assaulting Sword Beach and linking with 6th Airborne
notes: Landed at Sword; relieved Pegasus Bridge garrison at ~19:00 and linked with 6th Airborne; D-Day objective Caen not taken.

current_activity: advancing on Caen; halted by 21st Panzer counterattack
notes: KSLI reached Biéville-Beuville near Caen with few supporting weapons and exposed flanks; assault halted by 21st Panzer Division counter-attack.

current_activity: Charnwood: clears the Lebisey area and, with the 33rd Armoured Brigade, takes the high ground round Point 64 above Caen
notes: Event date: 8 July 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 313, 315). Event definition: On the first day of the attack on Caen the division completely clears the Lebisey area and, supported in the early evening by the 33rd Armoured Brigade, captures the high ground round Point 64, from which it overlooks Caen; patrols reach the outskirts but debris stops them (p. 315); on 9 July it moves into Caen (p. 316). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 313: "At 4.20 a.m. on July the 8th the full force of the artillery came down"; p. 315: "British Division had completely cleared the Lebisey area and, apart from some heavy shelling and mortaring from east of the Orne and a short-lived tank sortie against Hérouville, were not seriously im- peded. In the early evening, supported by the 33rd Armoured Brigade, they captured the high ground round Point 64 and were then overlooking Caen". Location: Lebisey / Biéville-Beuville approach to Caen (existing place PL0040) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the Lebisey approach to Caen, the first objective of the day. Location support: Ellis names the Lebisey area and Point 64 (p. 315).

current_activity: Goodwood: attacks at 07:45 on the east flank and takes Sannerville and Banneville by midday; Troarn holds out
notes: Event date: 18 July 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, p. 343). Event definition: The division, with the 152nd Brigade of the 51st Division under command and the 27th Armoured Brigade in support, advances at 07:45 behind a barrage; Sannerville and Banneville-la-Campagne, well hit by the bombing, fall soon after midday, Touffreville holds out until the evening and Troarn is still strongly defended at nightfall (p. 343). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 343: "the British 3rd Infantry Division of I Corps, with a brigade (152nd) of the 51st Division under command and sup- ported by the 27th Armoured Brigade, moved forward at 7.45 a.m."; "Sannerville and Banneville la Campagne had been well hit and their dazed defenders could offer little resistance; both were in British hands soon after midday". Location: Sannerville, Calvados (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Ellis names Sannerville as taken by midday (p. 343).

current_activity: Blockbuster: takes Kervenheim on the XXX Corps front, then heads for Winnekendonk
notes: Event date: 1 March 1945 (Ellis, vol. II, p. 273). Event definition: On 26 February XXX Corps' 3rd and 53rd Divisions attack on the Weeze-Kevelaer line while II Canadian Corps opens Blockbuster; the British 3rd Division takes Kervenheim on 1 March and then heads for Winnekendonk, which it is to gain two days later; the 3rd Division had relieved the 15th Division, which was withdrawn to reserve after the corps front had been carried to within two miles of Weeze (pp. 271 and 273). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 273: "XXX Corps' grd and 53rd Divisions attacked on the Weeze"; "the British grd Division had taken Kervenheim on March the 1st". Location: Kervenheim, North Rhine-Westphalia (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is the town of Kervenheim; the division headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names Kervenheim as the town taken (p. 273).

current_activity: Advance to the Elbe: crosses the Ems bridge and attacks Lingen from the north; the town falls on 6 April
notes: Event date: 6 April 1945 (Ellis, vol. II, p. 307). Event definition: The 3rd Division, following behind the Guards, crosses the Ems bridge taken on 3 April and, attacking Lingen from the north, hits the rear of a battalion of the Panzer Training Regiment Grossdeutschland and captures the commanding officer and his staff, which quickens the capture of the town; the German 7th Parachute Division is also met and Lingen falls after hard fighting only on 6 April, after which XXX Corps can press on towards Cloppenburg; for the time being the 3rd Division now joins XII Corps (p. 307). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 307: "The 3rd Division, following behind the Guards, crossed this bridge and, attacking Lingen from the north"; "it fell, after hard fighting, only on April the 6th"; "For the time being the grd Division now joined XII Corps". Location: Lingen (Ems), Niedersachsen (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is the town centre of Lingen; the division attacked from the north and its headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names Lingen as the town attacked from the north (p. 307).

current_activity: Bremen: from 20 April closes in round the city with three other divisions of XXX Corps; patches of stiff opposition
notes: Event date: 20 April 1945 (the day from which the divisions closed in) (Ellis, vol. II, p. 316). Event definition: From 20 April the four infantry divisions of XXX Corps (the 3rd, 43rd, 51st and 52nd) close in round the city of Bremen, finding patches of stiff opposition, especially on the high ground in the north, where 83 Group of the Royal Air Force helps to loosen some of the enemy positions; the fighting continues through the next five days, and on the 25th, after heavy and medium bomber attacks, the city itself is assaulted with the support of two heavy and four medium regiments of artillery (p. 316); the page does not say which part of the ring the division held. Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 316: "From the 2oth of April the four infantry divisions of XXX Corps (grd, 43rd, 51st and 52nd) closed in round the city of Bremen"; "find- ing patches of stiff opposition, especially on high ground in the north". Location: Bremen (existing place PL0625), the city the four divisions closed in on with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is the city of Bremen, which the four divisions encircled; the page gives no sector for the division and its headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names Bremen as the city the four divisions closed in round (p. 316).
